label: Exponential growth; fleets still small
rationale: Humanoids crossed from pilot to commercial deployment in 2025: Agility Digit at GXO moved 100,000+ totes and Figure 02 completed an 11-month BMW run. But single-site fleets remain small (2–10 units typical) and Tesla abandoned its 5,000 Optimus target; the report's summary table rates the KPI 🟡.

label: Approaching, not yet achieved
rationale: San Francisco is closest with robotaxis at ~50% of licensed taxis, and Waymo reached 450,000+ weekly rides, but Uber/Lyft still dominate and including rideshare robotaxis are <5% everywhere. All deployments are geofenced L4.

label: Distant
rationale: No robot has made coffee in a random unseen home; the closest result is π₀.5 performing cleaning tasks in unseen homes, and Figure's Helix grasping novel objects. Zero-shot reliability of ~20–50% is the core blocker, with the full test likely 2027–2030.

label: Approaching
rationale: Autonomous navigation, radiation survival and valve/switch manipulation have been demonstrated, but critical disaster-zone manipulation remains teleoperated and autonomous repair decisions are not demonstrated. TEPCO has retrieved only ~0.9 g of the ~880 t of fuel debris.

label: Approaching
rationale: No humanoid has completed a verified continuous 8-hour fully autonomous shift; Figure 02 ran 10-hour shifts for 11 months at BMW but required support staff. Deployments remain limited to 1–2 repetitive tasks, need human resets, and Optimus demos are often teleoperated.
